title: Fraction strips at the kitchen table
why: Sam can match fractions when they are pictures. This helps connect the picture to the numbers that go with it.
steps: Cut four paper strips the same length.
Leave the first one whole. Fold the others into 2, 4, and 8 equal parts and mark the folds.
Line up the strips. Ask: how many of the small parts cover the same space as one half?
Write the pair you find together, like 1/2 = 4/8.

title: Halves and quarters while you cook
why: Everyday measuring gives Sam a reason to use the same idea outside of schoolwork.
steps: Ask Sam to fill the 1/2 cup, then find how many 1/4 cups fill the same amount.
Say the sentence out loud together: two quarters make one half.
Try it once more with 1/3 and 1/6 if you have those cups.

title: Small-group number line placement
why: Classroom activity. Not shown to families.
steps: Place cards on the shared number line and defend the placement.

title: Fraction war with playing cards
why: Ava is ready to stretch. Comparing fractions with different bottoms keeps it interesting.
steps: Each player flips two cards and makes a fraction.
The larger fraction wins the round.
If they look close, draw a quick picture to check.
